From d702c3408213bb12bd570bb97204d8340d141c51 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Lukas Wunner <lukas@wunner.de>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 12:58:18 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] X.509: Fix out-of-bounds access when parsing extensions

Leo reports an out-of-bounds access when parsing a certificate with
empty Basic Constraints or Key Usage extension because the first byte of
the extension is read before checking its length.  Fix it.

The bug can be triggered by an unprivileged user by submitting a
specially crafted certificate to the kernel through the keyrings(7) API.
Leo has demonstrated this with a proof-of-concept program responsibly
disclosed off-list.

Fixes: 30eae2b037af ("KEYS: X.509: Parse Basic Constraints for CA")
Fixes: 567671281a75 ("KEYS: X.509: Parse Key Usage")
Reported-by: Leo Lin <leo@depthfirst.com> # off-list
Signed-off-by: Lukas Wunner <lukas@wunner.de>
Reviewed-by: Ignat Korchagin <ignat@linux.win>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # v6.4+
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

diff --git a/crypto/asymmetric_keys/x509_cert_parser.c b/crypto/asymmetric_keys/x509_cert_parser.c
index 37e4fb9da106..bfd10f0195e0 100644
--- a/crypto/asymmetric_keys/x509_cert_parser.c
+++ b/crypto/asymmetric_keys/x509_cert_parser.c
@@ -609,10 +609,10 @@ int x509_process_extension(void *context, size_t hdrlen,
 		 *   0x04 is where keyCertSign lands in this bit string
 		 *   0x80 is where digitalSignature lands in this bit string
 		 */
-		if (v[0] != ASN1_BTS)
-			return -EBADMSG;
 		if (vlen < 4)
 			return -EBADMSG;
+		if (v[0] != ASN1_BTS)
+			return -EBADMSG;
 		if (v[2] >= 8)
 			return -EBADMSG;
 		if (v[3] & 0x80)
@@ -645,10 +645,10 @@ int x509_process_extension(void *context, size_t hdrlen,
 		 *	(Expect 0xFF if the CA is TRUE)
 		 * vlen should match the entire extension size
 		 */
-		if (v[0] != (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ))
-			return -EBADMSG;
 		if (vlen < 2)
 			return -EBADMSG;
+		if (v[0] != (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ))
+			return -EBADMSG;
 		if (v[1] != vlen - 2)
 			return -EBADMSG;
 		/* Empty SEQUENCE means CA:FALSE (default value omitted per DER) */
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes two out-of-bounds access vulnerabilities in the X.509 certificate parser, both located in the `x509_process_extension()` function in `crypto/asymmetric_keys/x509_cert_parser.c`. Each vulnerability stems from the same logical flaw: the code checks the first byte of a TLV extension value (`v[0]`) before verifying that the value length (`vlen`) is sufficient to access that byte. The fix swaps the order of these checks—moving the length validation before the byte check—for both the Key Usage and Basic Constraints extension parsers. This ensures no out-of-bounds read occurs when processing malformed certificates with empty or overly short extensions.

**Changes per file:**

- **`crypto/asymmetric_keys/x509_cert_parser.c`:**
  - **Key Usage extension parsing** (lines originally 609-613): Reorder so that `vlen < 4` is checked before `v[0] != ASN1_BTS`.
  - **Basic Constraints extension parsing** (lines originally 645-649): Reorder so that `vlen < 2` is checked before `v[0] != (ASN1_CONS_BIT | ASN1_SEQ)`.

**Relationship between modifications:**

Both modifications address the identical root cause—an unchecked length before dereferencing `v[0]`—in adjacent sections of the same function for two distinct certificate extensions. They are logically independent but share the same fix pattern, ensuring that the parser safely handles extension values that may start at an insufficiently sized buffer.
